source_text:
Qui non odit patrem…
Uxorem virginem de populo suo accipiat. Ecclesia virgo casta Christo. Non vidua haeresum.
thought_title: The high priest's marriage as the Church's chastity
orientation: Origen is interpreting the high priest's marriage rules from Leviticus 21, applying them spiritually to Christ and the Church.
pass_a_gloss: Who [does] not hate [his] father… [Let him] take a wife [who is] a virgin from his [own] people. [The] Church [is] a virgin pure to Christ. Not [a] widow of heresies.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of the Levitical requirement, which Origen immediately applies spiritually.
rejected: a wife who is a virgin

choices.why: Preserves the possessive and the source restriction, which matters for the spiritual reading of the Church as Christ's own.

choices.english: The Church is a chaste virgin for Christ
choices.why: Supplies the copula to make the terse Latin application clear in English while keeping the word order and the dative of reference.
rejected: The Church, a chaste virgin, to Christ
A chaste virgin Church for Christ

choices.why: Keeps the genitive 'of heresies' to show the Church is not bereft of the true faith and married to error.

bible_refs.note: Uxorem virginem de populo suo accipiat

pass_b_english: Whoever does not hate father… Let him take a virgin wife from his own people (Leviticus 21:13-14). The Church is a chaste virgin for Christ. Not a widow of heresies.

last_rejected.why: Missing 'mother' and 'wife/children' from Luke 14:26 allusion; also 'hate' is Christ's command, not Levitical law.
last_rejected.fix: Whoever does not hate father and mother, wife and children… (Luke 14:26).
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'Qui non odit patrem…' has ellipsis; translator faithfully renders truncated text, not full Luke 14:26.

last_rejected.quote: Let him take a virgin wife from his own people (Leviticus 21:13-14).
last_rejected.source_quote: Uxorem virginem de populo suo accipiat.
last_rejected.why: Missing 'et' and broader context: high priest must marry virgin, not widow/divorced/prostitute.
last_rejected.fix: Let him take a virgin wife from his own people, neither a widow, nor divorced, nor defiled, a harlot (Lev 21:13-14).
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'Uxorem virginem de populo suo accipiat' lacks 'et'; citation Lev 21:13-14 supplies context. No source words omitted.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'Not a widow: heresies' or 'Not a widow of heresies'—but 'vidua haeresum' is genitive plural; English adds article 'a' making it sound like one widow.
last_rejected.ruling: 'a widow' is normal English rendering of singular 'vidua'; article required by English grammar, not meaning-changing addition.
